A.summary: Ormond, Lord Lieutenant at Dublin, writes to his son Arran in London about William Douglas, a Scottish preacher whose tale of a covenanting rising had come to nothing. Two names and a clause are in figures, set as a trial of Arran's skill in deciphering; the figures say that if Douglas is right someone and the King are in some danger or plot, 'but it seems to Ormond not credible'.
